rule_findings.title: Successful login after repeated failures
rule_findings.description: 6 failed logins from 10.0.5.23 were followed by a successful login for admin within 10 minutes.

rule_findings.title: Successful login at unusual hour
rule_findings.description: admin logged in from 10.0.5.23 at 02:14. Review indicator, not proof of compromise.

rule_findings.title: Sudo activity after suspicious login
rule_findings.description: admin ran sudo (/usr/bin/cat /etc/shadow) shortly after a suspicious login. This shows sudo use, not confirmed privilege escalation.

summary: The scenario involves a series of failed SSH login attempts followed by a successful login, with subsequent sudo activity. The unusual login timing is also noted.

attack_chain.explanation: The failed login attempts from 10.0.5.23 to the admin account are indicative of an attack.
The successful login for admin followed by sudo activity is a clear indication of an attacker.
The unusual login timing (02:14) is correlated with the successful login and sudo activity.

mitigations: Implement strong authentication mechanisms such as multi-factor authentication.
Monitor and log SSH login attempts and successful logins for anomalies.
Restrict sudo usage to specific commands and users to prevent privilege escalation.
Review and update SSH configuration to use stronger encryption and disable password authentication.
Implement intrusion detection systems (IDS) to alert on suspicious login activities.
